patch_description:
The second program achieved the best score (0.91) with 50 parameters by splitting the reverse chain into odd and even parameter variants (crz_rev_a and crz_rev_b). The current program simplified this to a single cry_rev parameter, which reduced the score to 0.90.

This edit restores the beneficial parameter-splitting strategy while keeping CRY gates (instead of reverting to CRZ). The key insight is that odd-indexed and even-indexed reverse links ([7→6], [5→4], [3→2], [1→0] vs [6→5], [4→3], [2→1]) may benefit from different learned parameters.

By using two parameters instead of one, we provide the model with richer expressivity while maintaining parameter efficiency (only adding 1 parameter). This should tighten the generalization gap and improve validation/test accuracy without significantly increasing training time or depth.
